hints: Count the hydrogen atoms on each side.
There are 2 oxygen atoms on the left. How many are on the right?
Try putting a 2 in front of H₂O.
Count the nitrogen atoms on each side.
You need 2 nitrogen atoms on the right. What coefficient gives you that?
Put a 2 in front of NH₃, then balance hydrogen.
How many chlorine atoms are on the left?
You have 2 Cl on the left but only 1 on the right.
Put a 2 in front of NaCl, then balance Na.
Count each element on both sides.
This equation might already be balanced!
All coefficients are 1 — it's already balanced.
Count the oxygen atoms on each side.
2 oxygen on the left, only 1 on the right.
Put a 2 in front of MgO, then balance Mg.
The product has both Fe and O — balance one element at a time.
Start with Fe₂O₃ having a coefficient of 2 to get even numbers.
4Fe + 3O₂ → 2Fe₂O₃. Try coefficient 4 for Fe.
This is similar to the iron oxide equation.
The product has 3 oxygens but O₂ comes in pairs of 2.
Put 2 in front of Al₂O₃, then balance Al and O.
Count the oxygen atoms on each side.
O₂ has 2 oxygens, CaO has 1.
Put 2 in front of CaO, then balance Ca.
The product has 5 oxygens — an odd number. Try doubling the product.
With 2 P₂O₅ you need 10 oxygens, so 5 O₂.
4P + 5O₂ → 2P₂O₅.
N₂ has 2 nitrogens. How many Li₃N do you need to have 2 N?
Put 2 in front of Li₃N → you need 6 Li on the left.
6Li + N₂ → 2Li₃N.
Count the oxygen atoms on each side.
Right side: H₂O has 1 O, O₂ has 2 O → total 3. Left side has 2.
Put 2 in front of H₂O₂ and 2 in front of H₂O.
Focus on oxygen — it has 3 in the reactant but comes in pairs on the right.
2 KClO₃ gives 6 oxygens. 3 O₂ also gives 6.
2KClO₃ → 2KCl + 3O₂.
NaN₃ has 3 nitrogens, but N₂ comes in pairs.
With 2 NaN₃ you get 6 N. You need 3 N₂ to match.
2NaN₃ → 2Na + 3N₂.
Count the oxygen atoms on each side.
O₂ has 2 oxygens. H₂O only has 1.
Put 2 in front of H₂O and 2 in front of H₂.
Count hydrogen: 4 on the left, 2 per H₂O on the right.
Put 2 in front of H₂O for 4 H. Check oxygen now.
NH₄NO₃ → N₂O + 2H₂O. Check: N=2|2, H=4|4, O=3|3.
ZnCl₂ needs 2 chlorines. How many does HCl give you?
Put 2 in front of HCl to get 2 Cl and 2 H.
Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl₂ + H₂.
Count each element on both sides.
This equation is already balanced!
All coefficients are 1.
MgCl₂ needs 2 chlorines.
Put 2 in front of HCl.
Mg + 2HCl → MgCl₂ + H₂.
AlCl₃ has 3 Cl but H₂ needs even H. Try balancing Cl first.
2 AlCl₃ needs 6 Cl → 6 HCl → 6 H → 3 H₂.
2Al + 6HCl → 2AlCl₃ + 3H₂.
Balance C first, then H, then O.
1 C on each side. 4 H left → 2 H₂O right.
CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O.
Count each element on both sides.
H: NaOH has 1 + HCl has 1 = 2 on left. H₂O has 2 on right.
It's already balanced! All coefficients are 1.
Count all elements on each side.
Ag, N, O, Na, Cl — they all match 1:1.
Already balanced. All coefficients are 1.
Count Na: 2 on left, 1 per NaCl on right.
Put 2 in front of NaCl for 2 Na and 2 Cl.
BaCl₂ + Na₂SO₄ → BaSO₄ + 2NaCl.
PbI₂ needs 2 iodines. How many KI?
2 KI gives 2 I and 2 K. You need 2 KNO₃ for the K.
Pb(NO₃)₂ + 2KI → PbI₂ + 2KNO₃.
Na₂SO₄ needs 2 Na. NaOH only has 1.
Put 2 in front of NaOH. Now count H and O.
H₂SO₄ + 2NaOH → Na₂SO₄ + 2H₂O.
Ca(OH)₂ needs 2 oxygens. Each H₂O has 1.
Put 2 in front of H₂O. Count H: 4 left, 2+2=4 right.
Ca + 2H₂O → Ca(OH)₂ + H₂.
Balance C first: 2 C left → 2 CO₂ right.
Balance H: 6 H left → 3 H₂O right. Now count O on right: 4+3=7.
2C₂H₆ + 7O₂ → 4CO₂ + 6H₂O.
Balance C first: 3 C → 3 CO₂.
Balance H: 8 H → 4 H₂O. Count O on right: 6+4=10.
C₃H₈ + 5O₂ → 3CO₂ + 4H₂O.
Balance C: 2 → 2 CO₂. Balance H: 6 → 3 H₂O.
O on right: 4+3=7. O on left: 1 + 2x = 7 → x=3.
C₂H₅OH + 3O₂ → 2CO₂ + 3H₂O.
Balance C: 6 → 6 CO₂. Balance H: 12 → 6 H₂O.
O on right: 12+6=18. O on left: 6 + 2x = 18 → x=6.
C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ → 6CO₂ + 6H₂O.
Fe₂O₃ has 2 Fe → need 2 FeCl₃.
2 FeCl₃ needs 6 Cl → 6 HCl. 6 H → 3 H₂O.
Fe₂O₃ + 6HCl → 2FeCl₃ + 3H₂O.
Al₂O₃ needs 2 Al on the left.
Fe₂O₃ has 2 Fe → need 2 Fe on the right.
2Al + Fe₂O₃ → Al₂O₃ + 2Fe.
Na₂CO₃ has 2 Na → need 2 NaCl.
2 NaCl needs 2 Cl → 2 HCl.
Na₂CO₃ + 2HCl → 2NaCl + H₂O + CO₂.
N₂O₅ has 5 oxygens — odd number. Try doubling.
2 N₂O₅ = 10 O → 5 O₂. 4 N → 2 N₂.
2N₂ + 5O₂ → 2N₂O₅.
Count H: H₂O has 2, KOH has 1, H₂ has 2.
Try 2K + 2H₂O → 2KOH + H₂.
Balance C: 4 → 4 CO₂. Balance H: 10 → 5 H₂O.
O on right: 8+5=13 — odd! Double everything.
2C₄H₁₀ + 13O₂ → 8CO₂ + 10H₂O.
CaCl₂ needs 2 Cl → 2 HCl.
2 H from 2 HCl → 1 H₂O. Check O: 3 left, 1+2=3 right.
CaCO₃ + 2HCl → CaCl₂ + H₂O + CO₂.
Count each element on both sides.
Everything already matches 1:1.
Already balanced.
2 Al left → 2 Al(OH)₃. 3 S left → 3 Na₂SO₄.
3 Na₂SO₄ needs 6 Na → 6 NaOH.
Al₂(SO₄)₃ + 6NaOH → 2Al(OH)₃ + 3Na₂SO₄.
2 Fe → 2 Fe(OH)₃. 3 S → 3 K₂SO₄.
3 K₂SO₄ needs 6 K → 6 KOH.
Fe₂(SO₄)₃ + 6KOH → 2Fe(OH)₃ + 3K₂SO₄.
Balance C: 2 → 2 CO₂. Balance H: 2 → 1 H₂O.
O on right: 4+1=5 — odd! Double everything.
2C₂H₂ + 5O₂ → 4CO₂ + 2H₂O.
Balance C: 6 → 6 CO₂. Balance H: 6 → 3 H₂O.
O on right: 12+3=15 — odd! Double everything.
2C₆H₆ + 15O₂ → 12CO₂ + 6H₂O.
Count each element on both sides.
Already balanced.
Fe₂O₃ has 3 O → need 3 MgO.
3 MgO needs 3 Mg. Fe₂O₃ has 2 Fe → 2 Fe.
3Mg + Fe₂O₃ → 3MgO + 2Fe.
FeCl₃ has 3 Cl but Cl₂ comes in pairs.
2 FeCl₃ = 6 Cl → 3 Cl₂. And 2 Fe.
2Fe + 3Cl₂ → 2FeCl₃.
Count each element carefully.
Already balanced.
Mg(OH)₂ needs 2 OH → 2 NaOH.
2 NaOH gives 2 Na → 2 NaCl. 2 Cl = MgCl₂.
MgCl₂ + 2NaOH → Mg(OH)₂ + 2NaCl.
Balance C: 5 → 5 CO₂. Balance H: 12 → 6 H₂O.
C₅H₁₂ + 8O₂ → 5CO₂ + 6H₂O.
Ca₃(PO₄)₂ needs 3 Ca → 3 Ca(OH)₂. And 2 P → 2 H₃PO₄.
3Ca(OH)₂ + 2H₃PO₄ → Ca₃(PO₄)₂ + 6H₂O.
Balance C: 8 → 8 CO₂. Balance H: 18 → 9 H₂O.
O on right: 16+9=25. Odd! Double everything.
2C₈H₁₈ + 25O₂ → 16CO₂ + 18H₂O.
Start by balancing the iron atoms on both sides.
2 Fe₂O₃ gives 4 Fe on the left. Put 4 in front of Fe on the right.
2Fe₂O₃ + 3C → 4Fe + 3CO₂.
Look at the oxygen atoms in Al₂O₃ — you need 3.
3 CuO gives 3 O and 3 Cu. Al₂O₃ needs 2 Al.
2Al + 3CuO → Al₂O₃ + 3Cu.
This is a decomposition reaction — check if it is already balanced.
Count each element: Ca, C, and O on both sides.
CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂ is already balanced with all coefficients of 1.
Hydrogen appears in three places — count carefully.
Try 2 Na and 2 H₂O on the left, then 2 NaOH on the right.
2Na + 2H₂O → 2NaOH + H₂.
MgCl₂ has 2 Cl atoms — how many HCl do you need?
2 HCl gives 2 Cl and 2 H. H₂ accounts for 2 H.
Mg + 2HCl → MgCl₂ + H₂.
Start with Cl: AlCl₃ has 3 Cl. Balance Cl first.
2 AlCl₃ needs 6 Cl → 6 HCl. 6 H → 3 H₂. 2 Al on left.
2Al + 6HCl → 2AlCl₃ + 3H₂.
Fe₂O₃ has 2 Fe — put 2 in front of Fe on the right.
3 CO picks up oxygen to become 3 CO₂. Check O: 3+3=6, right: 6.
Fe₂O₃ + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO₂.
O₂ has 2 oxygen atoms but CuO only has 1.
Put 2 in front of CuO to use both oxygens.
2Cu + O₂ → 2CuO.
O₂ provides 2 oxygen atoms, but MgO only uses 1.
Double the MgO to use both oxygens, then match Mg.
2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO.
Fe₂O₃ has 3 O, but O₂ has 2. Find the LCM of 2 and 3.
LCM is 6: 3 O₂ = 6 O, 2 Fe₂O₃ = 6 O. Then 4 Fe on the left.
4Fe + 3O₂ → 2Fe₂O₃.
Balance C first: 1 CH₄ → 1 CO₂.
4 H in CH₄ → 2 H₂O. Total O on right: 2+2=4, so 2 O₂.
CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O.
Balance C: 2 C → 2 CO₂. Then H: 6 H → 3 H₂O.
O on right: 4+3=7, which is odd. Double everything to clear the fraction.
2C₂H₆ + 7O₂ → 4CO₂ + 6H₂O.
Balance C: 3 C → 3 CO₂. Balance H: 8 H → 4 H₂O.
O on right: 6+4=10. So 5 O₂ on the left.
C₃H₈ + 5O₂ → 3CO₂ + 4H₂O.
Balance C: 4 C → 4 CO₂. Balance H: 8 H → 4 H₂O.
O on right: 8+4=12. So 6 O₂ on the left.
C₄H₈ + 6O₂ → 4CO₂ + 4H₂O.
Balance C: 2 C → 2 CO₂. Balance H: 4 H → 2 H₂O.
O on right: 4+2=6. So 3 O₂ on the left.
C₂H₄ + 3O₂ → 2CO₂ + 2H₂O.
Balance C: 2 C → 2 CO₂. Balance H: 2 H → 1 H₂O.
O on right: 4+1=5, which is odd. Double everything.
2C₂H₂ + 5O₂ → 4CO₂ + 2H₂O.
Balance C: 3 C → 3 CO₂. Balance H: 6 H → 3 H₂O.
O on right: 6+3=9, which is odd. Double everything.
2C₃H₆ + 9O₂ → 6CO₂ + 6H₂O.
CH₃OH has C, 4 H, and 1 O. Balance C first, then H.
2 CH₃OH → 2 CO₂ + 4 H₂O. O right: 4+4=8. O left: 2+6=8. So 3 O₂.
2CH₃OH + 3O₂ → 2CO₂ + 4H₂O.
C₂H₅OH has 2 C, 6 H, and 1 O. Balance C → 2 CO₂.
6 H → 3 H₂O. O right: 4+3=7. O left: 1+2x=7, x=3.
C₂H₅OH + 3O₂ → 2CO₂ + 3H₂O.
C₃H₇OH has 3 C, 8 H, and 1 O. Balance C → 3 CO₂.
8 H → 4 H₂O. O right: 6+4=10. O left: 1+2x=10 → x=4.5. Double all.
2C₃H₇OH + 9O₂ → 6CO₂ + 8H₂O.
ZnCl₂ needs 2 Cl atoms. How many HCl do you need?
2 HCl → 2 H and 2 Cl. The 2 H become H₂.
Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl₂ + H₂.
Iron displaces copper. Check if atoms are already balanced.
Fe:1=1, Cu:1=1, S:1=1, O:4=4. It is balanced!
Fe + CuSO₄ → FeSO₄ + Cu (all coefficients are 1).
Zinc displaces copper from the sulfate. Count each element.
Zn:1=1, Cu:1=1, S:1=1, O:4=4 — balanced as is.
Zn + CuSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Cu (all coefficients are 1).
Cl in FeCl₂ is 2, in AlCl₃ is 3. Find LCM of 2 and 3.
LCM=6: 3 FeCl₂ = 6 Cl, 2 AlCl₃ = 6 Cl. Then 2 Al and 3 Fe.
2Al + 3FeCl₂ → 2AlCl₃ + 3Fe.
Cu(NO₃)₂ has 2 N and 6 O. That means 2 AgNO₃.
2 AgNO₃ → 2 Ag. Cu is already 1 on each side.
Cu + 2AgNO₃ → Cu(NO₃)₂ + 2Ag.
SnCl₂ needs 2 Cl — use 2 HCl.
2 HCl gives 2 H → 1 H₂. Sn is balanced at 1.
Sn + 2HCl → SnCl₂ + H₂.
Pb(NO₃)₂ has 2 nitrate groups — you need 2 AgNO₃.
2 AgNO₃ → 2 Ag on the right. Pb:1=1.
Pb + 2AgNO₃ → Pb(NO₃)₂ + 2Ag.
FeCl₂ needs 2 Cl → 2 HCl.
2 H from HCl → 1 H₂. Fe is 1 on each side.
Fe + 2HCl → FeCl₂ + H₂.
Mg(NO₃)₂ has 2 nitrate groups — use 2 AgNO₃.
Mg + 2AgNO₃ → Mg(NO₃)₂ + 2Ag.
Cl: CuCl₂ has 2, AlCl₃ has 3. Find LCM of 2 and 3.
LCM=6: 3 CuCl₂ → 6 Cl, 2 AlCl₃ → 6 Cl. Then 2 Al and 3 Cu.
2Al + 3CuCl₂ → 2AlCl₃ + 3Cu.
This is a simple neutralization. Check if it is already balanced.
NaOH + HCl → NaCl + H₂O (all coefficients are 1).
K₂SO₄ needs 2 K — use 2 KOH.
H: 2+2=4 on left, 2×2=4 on right. O: 2+4=6 left, 4+2=6 right.
2KOH + H₂SO₄ → K₂SO₄ + 2H₂O.
CaCl₂ needs 2 Cl → 2 HCl.
H: 2+2=4 left, 2×2=4 right. O: 2 left, 2 right.
Ca(OH)₂ + 2HCl → CaCl₂ + 2H₂O.
BaCl₂ needs 2 Cl → 2 HCl.
H: 2+2=4 left, 2×2=4 right. O: 2 left, 2 right.
Ba(OH)₂ + 2HCl → BaCl₂ + 2H₂O.
Na₃PO₄ needs 3 Na → 3 NaOH.
H: 3+3=6 left, 2×3=6 right. O: 3+4=7 left, 4+3=7 right.
3NaOH + H₃PO₄ → Na₃PO₄ + 3H₂O.
Mg(NO₃)₂ needs 2 N → 2 HNO₃.
H: 2+2=4 left, 2×2=4 right. O: 2+6=8 left, 6+2=8 right.
Mg(OH)₂ + 2HNO₃ → Mg(NO₃)₂ + 2H₂O.
Al₂(SO₄)₃ needs 2 Al → 2 Al(OH)₃, and 3 S → 3 H₂SO₄.
2Al(OH)₃ + 3H₂SO₄ → Al₂(SO₄)₃ + 6H₂O.
Na₂CO₃ has 2 Na → 2 NaCl needs 2 Cl → 2 HCl.
H: 2 left, 2 right. C:1=1. O: 3 left, 1+2=3 right.
Na₂CO₃ + 2HCl → 2NaCl + H₂O + CO₂.
K₂CO₃ has 2 K → 2 KCl needs 2 Cl → 2 HCl.
H: 2 left, 2 right. C:1=1. O: 3 left, 1+2=3 right.
K₂CO₃ + 2HCl → 2KCl + H₂O + CO₂.
Ba₃(PO₄)₂ needs 3 Ba → 3 Ba(OH)₂, and 2 P → 2 H₃PO₄.
H: 6+6=12 left, 2×6=12 right. O: 6+8=14 left, 8+6=14 right.
3Ba(OH)₂ + 2H₃PO₄ → Ba₃(PO₄)₂ + 6H₂O.
Balance N first: match NH₃ and NO coefficients.
4 NH₃ → 4 NO + 6 H₂O. O right: 4+6=10, so 5 O₂.
4NH₃ + 5O₂ → 4NO + 6H₂O.
Fe₂O₃ has 2 Fe → 2 Fe on the right.
3 O in Fe₂O₃ → 3 CO needs 3 C.
Fe₂O₃ + 3C → 2Fe + 3CO.
Al₂(SO₄)₃ needs 2 Al and 3 SO₄ → 3 CuSO₄.
2Al + 3CuSO₄ → Al₂(SO₄)₃ + 3Cu.
Mg₃N₂ has 3 Mg and 2 N. N₂ already has 2 N.
Use 3 Mg and 1 N₂. Check: Mg:3=3, N:2=2.
3Mg + N₂ → Mg₃N₂.
Al₂O₃ has 3 O, O₂ has 2. LCM of 2 and 3 is 6.
3 O₂ = 6 O → 2 Al₂O₃. Then 4 Al on the left.
4Al + 3O₂ → 2Al₂O₃.
Balance Cu first: 2 Cu₂S → 4 Cu left, 2 Cu₂O → 4 Cu right.
S: 2 left, 2 SO₂ right. O right: 2+4=6, so 3 O₂.
2Cu₂S + 3O₂ → 2Cu₂O + 2SO₂.
Fe₃O₄ needs 3 Fe and 4 O → 4 H₂O.
3Fe + 4H₂O → Fe₃O₄ + 4H₂.
This is a thermite-style reaction. O stays as 3 on each side.
Cr₂O₃ → 2 Cr. Al₂O₃ needs 2 Al.
Cr₂O₃ + 2Al → Al₂O₃ + 2Cr.
FeCl₃ has 3 Cl, Cl₂ has 2. LCM of 2 and 3 is 6.
3 Cl₂ = 6 Cl → 2 FeCl₃. Then 2 Fe on the left.
2Fe + 3Cl₂ → 2FeCl₃.
Balance O: Fe₃O₄ has 4, Al₂O₃ has 3. LCM of 4 and 3 is 12.
3 Fe₃O₄ = 12 O → 4 Al₂O₃. Then 8 Al and 9 Fe.
8Al + 3Fe₃O₄ → 4Al₂O₃ + 9Fe.
